title: Single sign-on
description: Let your people sign in through your identity provider (SAML 2.0, OpenID Connect or a custom OAuth 2.0 provider) and keep them in sync over SCIM.
copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the text and copy it by hand.

connections.title: Connections
connections.description: Each connection links one identity provider. A new connection starts off: turn it on when the provider is set up.
connections.none: No connections yet. Add one to let your people sign in with SSO.
connections.discoveryError: Provider metadata could not be fetched: {{error}}
connections.discoveryPending: Provider metadata is being fetched. Sign-in is unavailable until it arrives.
connections.testOff: Turn the connection on to test a sign-in.
connections.removeDescription: Nobody can sign in through it any more. Accounts stay; their SSO link to this connection is removed.
connections.created: Added {{name}}. It is off until you turn it on.
connections.oauth2Ready: Ready: an OAuth 2.0 connection has no provider metadata to fetch.
connections.oauth2Off: Turn it on to let people sign in: an OAuth 2.0 connection has no provider metadata to fetch.

form.description: Secrets and certificates are stored safely and never shown again.
form.name: Name
form.urlInvalid: Enter a full URL, starting with https://.
form.issuerHint: The provider’s OpenID Connect issuer. Its discovery document is fetched after saving.
form.secretKeep: Leave empty to keep the current secret.
form.metadataUrlHint: An https:// URL: fills in the fields below from the provider's metadata. Review them before saving.
form.idpEntityIdHint: What the provider names as the issuer of its assertions.
form.certificateHint: Only assertions signed by it are accepted.
form.certificateKeep: Leave empty to keep the current certificates.
form.nextCertificateHint: Add it while the provider rotates its certificate.
form.allowIdpInitiated: Accept sign-ins started by the provider
form.allowIdpInitiatedHint: Weaker against login CSRF. Leave off unless the provider can only start the sign-in itself.
form.jitHint: A person of a verified domain who is not a member yet joins with no roles.
form.enabledHint: Off, the connection signs nobody in.
form.presetHint: Fills in the endpoints and the response mapping. You can still edit them.
form.redirectHint: After saving, the connection shows the redirect URI to register at the provider.
form.redirectHintEdit: Register this redirect URI at the provider.
form.authorizationEndpointHint: Where the browser is sent to sign in.
form.tokenEndpointHint: Where the code is exchanged for an access token (PKCE is always on).
form.userinfoEndpointHint: Read once per sign-in with the access token.
form.authMethodHint: How the client proves itself at the token URL.
form.publicClient: A public client sends no secret.
form.scopesHint: Press Enter or a comma after each scope. None are asked for by default.
form.mappingHint: Where the user info answer holds the person. Paths are names joined by dots, like data.open_id.
form.mappingRootHint: Where the person is in the answer. Empty: the whole answer.
form.mappingSubjectHint: The provider’s stable id of the person, never an address.
form.mappingEmailHint: The address, in the user object.
form.mappingPictureHint: Read, but not stored: accounts have no picture.
form.mappingGroupsHint: An array of group names, read for the group roles.
form.mappingErrorCodeHint: A field of the whole answer that marks a failure (Lark answers 200 with code not 0).
form.emailTrustHint: Whether the provider vouches for the address.
form.emailVerifiedPathHint: A field of the user object that must be true.

domains.title: Email domains
domains.description: Only addresses of a verified domain sign in or are provisioned through SSO, so a tenant can’t claim someone else’s addresses.
domains.checking: Looking the record up. Reload in a moment to see the result.
domains.publish: Publish this DNS record, then check it.

scim.title: SCIM provisioning
scim.description: The identity provider creates, updates and deactivates people and groups over SCIM 2.0.
scim.step1: Make a role with the single permission “Provision SCIM” (Roles).
scim.step2: Create an API client with that role and copy its key (API clients).
scim.step3: Give the identity provider the base URL and the key as its bearer token.
scim.clients: API clients and their last call
scim.noClients: No API client yet, so no SCIM key either.
scim.noAccess: To see the API clients that hold the key, you need permission to manage API clients.

policy.title: Require SSO
policy.description: When on, members sign in to this workspace only through one of its connections.
policy.exemptionsHint: Exempted members can still sign in with a password or passkey (break-glass). Each use is audited.

mappings.title: Group roles of {{name}}
mappings.description: Give roles by the groups the identity provider lists. At every sign-in a person gets the roles of their groups and loses the ones a mapping gave whose group they left. Roles you give yourself stay.
mappings.attributeHint: Where the provider lists the groups. Empty: groups.
mappings.none: No mappings yet. Without mappings no roles are synced.
mappings.groupHint: Compared exactly: a name, or the group ID (Microsoft Entra ID sends IDs).
mappings.incomplete: Enter a group and choose a role.
mappings.oauth2Groups: This connection reads the groups from the “Groups path” of its response mapping. Edit the connection to change it.

exemption.title: Exempt a member
exemption.description: An exempted member can still sign in with a password or passkey while SSO is required. With two-factor on, only members who enrolled it can be exempted.
exemption.reasonHint: Why, for example an emergency administrator.

authMethod.client_secret_post: Client secret, in the request body

emailTrust.verified-domains: Trust addresses in our verified domains
emailTrust.neverExplain: The provider’s address is never taken as verified: a first sign-in is refused.
emailTrust.fieldExplain: The address counts as verified when the field below is exactly true.
emailTrust.verified-domainsExplain: The address counts as verified when its domain is one you verified here.
